findings.title: Update invalidation tests the org-wrapped `original` model, so its `isEnabled()` depends on org state and can skip a needed invalidation
findings.body: `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` receives `original` from `getById()`. With the ORGANIZATION feature on, that is the wrapped model whose `isEnabled()` also requires the organization to exist and be enabled. The cached `getForLogin` ID sets are built from the raw DB state and ignore org enabled-state. If an IDP is linked to a disabled org, is enabled and public in the DB, and is already in the cached set, `test(original)` is false. An update that hides it on login, marks it link-only or disables it makes `test(updated)` false too, so the method returns early and nothing is invalidated. The stale ID set keeps the IDP. When the org is re-enabled, `getForLogin` returns the fresh model through `getById`. The bean in this PR re-checks only `isEnabled()`, not `hideOnLogin` or `linkOnly`, so an IDP that was hidden or link-only appears on the login page. The comparison should use the raw persisted state, for example the delegate's model or one not wrapped by the org-aware `isEnabled`.

findings.title: remove() now always queries the DB for the IDP, even when it is in the cache
findings.body: `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` is now called unconditionally at the top of `remove()`. Previously the delegate was queried only when the alias key was invalidated; otherwise the cached entry supplied the internal id. The `else` branch's cache lookup no longer saves a query. The cached or already-loaded model could be used to decide whether login caches need invalidation.

findings.title: Cleanup registers removal of a literal IDP "alias" instead of the created IDPs
findings.body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` binds to an IDP with the literal alias "alias", not the `idp-alias-N` IDPs just created. The same mistake is at line 425 for `idp-alias-20`, and the new test copied it from `testCacheIDPByOrg`. The cleanup never removes the 21 IDPs and will probably hit a 404 for the nonexistent "alias" when it runs. The test asserts exact counts, so leftover IDPs would make it order-dependent if the realm is not re-imported between tests. The variable alias should be captured, for example `testRealm().identityProviders().get(alias)::remove`.

findings.title: No test for the positive invalidation paths of create/remove, or for the bean and org-disabled behaviour
findings.body: `testCacheIDPForLogin` covers only creating or removing IDPs that are not login-eligible, which must not invalidate. It never creates or removes an IDP that is login-eligible, though `create()` and `remove()` now call `registerIDPLoginInvalidation` to invalidate in that case. It also does not cover disabled orgs, where the cache holds IDs based on raw DB state but `getById` returns wrapped models. The `isEnabled()` re-check added to `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` has no test either. The cached results are never compared with what `getForLogin` actually returns.
